title: Your 10-minute game is a tech demo, and that's fine. Just call it that
author: ShelterSpirited4162
selftext:
I need to vent a bit.

Every day I scroll and see posts like "I made a full game in 10 minutes with AI" or "built this game in one evening." Then I open it and it's a 3D model that can walk around. No goal, no progression, no balancing, no menus, no save system, no sound design, nothing that makes it a game.

That's a prototype. Prototypes are cool. I make them too. But calling it a game is misleading, especially for beginners who start thinking they're doing something wrong because their project takes months.

For context: I've been working on my own game for months. Some days I spend a few hours just playtesting the same sections over and over. Fixing one bug creates two more. Tweaking movement until it feels right. Adjusting difficulty. Rewriting UI because it looked fine on my screen and broken on others. That's the part nobody posts about, and it's where most of the actual work is.

AI tools absolutely speed things up. I use them myself. But they speed up the first 10%. The last 90% is polish, testing and a lot of boring decisions, and no tool does that for you in 10 minutes.

So if you're grinding on your project for months and feeling slow because of these posts: you're not slow. That's just what making a game actually looks like.

I'll be sharing mine soon. Curious, how long did your "small" game actually take from first prototype to something you'd call finished?

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body:
When it has a beginning and an end, with mechanics and the ability to be played to completion. Tic-Tac-Toe is a game. Pong is a game. Both have less going on than many of the games being released around here.

The stuff here is just unpolished and took out of the oven way too soon. They're games, but they're unfinished.

comments.author: Ok-Sea300
comments.body:
You mean all of the "Claude made this game in 24 hours with one prompt! Gahyuck!" games that look flashy at the surface level in a quick fly-by-night screenshot but you can't leave the front yard because Claude cant really do that aren't real games?

Blowing my mind right now.

comments.author: barret232hxc
comments.body: i've never made a 10 minute game in my life? Via traditional game dev or ai game dev. Who is making anything that has less than 10 minutes?

comments.author: Reflexorz15
comments.body: Right. I just got past implementing important infrastructure, working dedicated servers and a very simple playable slice. It took me a month and 25 implementation plans later. This is my third time remaking my game on different frameworks after learning things as I went (after 6 months). While I don’t have the whole “game in 24hrs”, I know that I’m setting things up very carefully for the future to handle a bunch of data and a very large world for multiplayer. And I’m not blasting hundreds of dollars every month like some people are because I’m trying to save money. Makes me feel better that it feels like I’m doing it this way to where yes, I’m vibe coding, but I’m very carefully planning and testing for every implementation.

comments.author: tracylsteel
comments.body: I'm constantly looking at all these games or amazing 3D worlds made and am so amazed! I am still working on this ocean world, using blender and three.js with Opus 5.5 and no way is it like ten minutes as there's a lot of things to do like model wraps and stuff. By the way, any tips from anyone would be great! As far as gameplay is concerned, there are secrets to find [https://shimmerocean.com/](https://shimmerocean.com/)

comments.author: TheMarco
comments.body: It's also what makes all the haters think we just push a few buttons and a full game rolls out. It's rather infuriating to me. Real games take real work, even with AI.

comments.author: Alexguitar11
comments.body: I spent over 100 hours on my game so far, still lots to do in it though to make it have more depth

replies.author: FastestSparrowInTown
replies.body: And that’s how AI game development is going to take off. AI has gotten a bad reputation because of devs who don’t care about their games and just want to ship something fast. Putting in 100+ hours shows the opposite.
